scenes.tts: A target makes too little N G F for every neuron that reaches it. So which neurons get to live?
scenes.caption: A target makes too little NGF for every neuron that reaches it. So which neurons get to live?
scenes.visual: Title card: Too Little to Go Around. Many sympathetic axons reach one target; a few NGF dots drift out.
scenes.narration: A target makes too little NGF for every neuron that reaches it. So which neurons get to live?

scenes.tts: Start with what you already know. Sympathetic neurons live in small clusters of nerve cells called ganglia.
scenes.visual: A ganglion appears as a cluster of round cell bodies. Label: sympathetic ganglion.
scenes.narration: Start with what you already know. Sympathetic neurons live in small clusters of nerve cells called ganglia.

scenes.tts: They send axons to targets such as the eye, the salivary gland and the heart.
scenes.visual: Axons grow out from the ganglion to three labelled targets: eye, salivary gland, heart.
scenes.narration: They send axons to targets such as the eye, the salivary gland and the heart.

scenes.tts: Those targets release nerve growth factor, N G F. The target makes it, not the neurons.
scenes.caption: Those targets release nerve growth factor, NGF. The target makes it, not the neurons.
scenes.visual: NGF dots released from each target at a steady rate. Label: nerve growth factor (NGF), made by the target.
scenes.narration: Those targets release nerve growth factor, NGF. The target makes it, not the neurons.

scenes.tts: Neurons that get enough N G F live. Those that do not die through a pro-death gene called Bax.
scenes.caption: Neurons that get enough NGF live. Those that do not die through a pro-death gene called Bax.
scenes.visual: Well-fed neurons stay lit; neurons with few NGF dots fade. A small gate labelled Bax sits inside the fading cells.
scenes.narration: Neurons that get enough NGF live. Those that do not die through a pro-death gene called Bax.

scenes.tts: This is normal development, not damage. In many developing populations, roughly half the neurons die.
scenes.visual: A neuron-count bar falls across the death period. On screen: roughly half die in many developing populations. Schematic, not counts.
scenes.narration: This is normal development, not damage. In many developing populations, roughly half the neurons die.

scenes.tts: The neurotrophic hypothesis puts it in one line. Neurons compete for a limiting amount of neurotrophic factor for survival.
scenes.visual: The one line appears on screen in quotation marks.
scenes.narration: The neurotrophic hypothesis puts it in one line. Neurons compete for a limiting amount of neurotrophic factor for survival.

scenes.tts: Change the target, and the count follows. Give a chick embryo an extra limb, and fewer motor neurons on that side die.
scenes.visual: A chick embryo with a grafted extra limb; motor neurons on that side stay lit. Label: more target, more survivors.
scenes.narration: Change the target, and the count follows. Give a chick embryo an extra limb, and fewer motor neurons on that side die.

scenes.tts: So the size of the target sets roughly how many neurons can win.
scenes.visual: A dial labelled target size; as it turns up, more neurons stay lit.
scenes.narration: So the size of the target sets roughly how many neurons can win.

scenes.tts: But the hypothesis only says there is a contest. It does not say how the contest is decided.
scenes.visual: A question mark over the cluster of neurons.
scenes.narration: But the hypothesis only says there is a contest. It does not say how the contest is decided.

scenes.tts: It also leaves a second question open. How does the outcome set the fit between a target and its neurons?
scenes.visual: Two labels appear: number of survivors, and how densely they cover the target.
scenes.narration: It also leaves a second question open. How does the outcome set the fit between a target and its neurons?

scenes.tts: The answer here comes from one cell type. Sympathetic neurons of the mouse superior cervical ganglion.
scenes.visual: A mouse outline with a small ganglion in the neck highlighted. Label: superior cervical ganglion.
scenes.narration: The answer here comes from one cell type. Sympathetic neurons of the mouse superior cervical ganglion.

scenes.tts: That ganglion sits in the neck and supplies the head. Some experiments used cultured rat neurons.
scenes.visual: Axons from the neck ganglion run up into the head. Small inset: neurons in a culture dish, labelled rat.
scenes.narration: That ganglion sits in the neck and supplies the head. Some experiments used cultured rat neurons.

scenes.tts: Make a guess before going on. If a target can feed only some neurons, what decides which ones?
scenes.visual: On screen: what decides which ones? Pause and guess.
scenes.narration: Make a guess before going on. If a target can feed only some neurons, what decides which ones?

scenes.tts: Here is the idea this lesson builds. The target sets how many. The neurons decide which.
scenes.visual: A card: The target sets how many; the neurons decide which.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea this lesson builds. The target sets how many. The neurons decide which.

scenes.tts: Take neurons that are otherwise alike. A small lead can grow only if its signal rises faster than in proportion.
scenes.visual: Two matched neurons; a small lead bar grows into a large one. Label: faster than in proportion.
scenes.narration: Take neurons that are otherwise alike. A small lead can grow only if its signal rises faster than in proportion.

scenes.tts: In the published simulations, N G F raised its receptor, Track A, and lengthened each Track A signal, and both were needed for the neurons to separate.
scenes.caption: In the published simulations, NGF raised its receptor, TrkA, and lengthened each TrkA signal, and both were needed for the neurons to separate.
scenes.visual: Two arrows from NGF: one to more TrkA receptors, one to a longer-running signal timer. Label: published simulations, both needed.
scenes.narration: In the published simulations, NGF raised its receptor, TrkA, and lengthened each TrkA signal, and both were needed for the neurons to separate.

scenes.tts: In the proposed model, winners then speed the death of losers, through a receptor called p seventy five.
scenes.caption: In the proposed model, winners then speed the death of losers, through a receptor called p75.
scenes.visual: Strong neurons glow; a weak neighbour with p75 on its surface fades faster. Label: proposed model.
scenes.narration: In the proposed model, winners then speed the death of losers, through a receptor called p75.

scenes.tts: The rule has limits. It does not say where a neuron's first small lead comes from.
scenes.visual: A list titled limits appears. Item 1: where the first lead comes from.
scenes.narration: The rule has limits. It does not say where a neuron's first small lead comes from.

scenes.tts: Arriving early, branching more or sitting closer are all candidates. The rule amplifies a head start.
scenes.visual: Three small sketches: an early axon, a branched axon, a closer axon. Arrow: amplified.
scenes.narration: Arriving early, branching more or sitting closer are all candidates. The rule amplifies a head start.

scenes.tts: Faster than in proportion is needed, not enough: steady basal synthesis pulls neurons back together. And the rule does not cover chick motor neurons. They draw on several factors at once.
scenes.visual: Items 2 and 3 on the limits list: needed, not enough (basal synthesis pulls neurons back together); chick motor neurons, several factors.
scenes.narration: Faster than in proportion is needed, not enough: steady basal synthesis pulls neurons back together. And the rule does not cover chick motor neurons. They draw on several factors at once.

scenes.tts: Takeaway. A limited supply sets roughly how many survive. The neurons' own feedback decides which ones.
scenes.visual: End card: supply sets how many; feedback picks which.
scenes.narration: Takeaway. A limited supply sets roughly how many survive. The neurons' own feedback decides which ones.
